channel.title: Global Competition Review - Article Feed
channel.description: Latest articles from Global Competition Review (globalcompetitionreview.com)

item.title: UK parliamentary committee explores potential outbound screening regime
item.description: An influential parliamentary committee is seeking views on the “merits and risks” of establishing an outbound investment screening regime targeting UK projects overseas, including in China.

item.title: Apple set to learn its fate in ACM dating app case
item.description: The Dutch competition authority will decide before the end of this month whether Apple must comply with a postponed order challenging commission rates imposed on dating app providers – with potential multi-million-euro fines on the cards if it fails to fall in line.

item.title: Seatgeek CEO: Exclusive deals industry “standard”
item.description: Live Nation has argued that its primary ticketing rival, SeatGeek, also mandates exclusivity from venues that host concerts and sporting events.

item.title: Friday night lights: The Tipline for 6 March 2026
item.description: Antitrust issues are not just plaguing collegiate sports. Software company Hudl has been accused of locking nearly 20,000 US high schools into its sports video analytics monopoly by acquiring 18 adjacent companies since 2011. Also in Tipline, President Donald Trump railed against NCAA v Alston during his “Saving College Sports” roundtable.

item.title: Lateral movement: The Briefing for 9 March 2026
item.description: Taylor Wessing, Hausfeld and Garrigues have announced new senior hires across London, Amsterdam and Brussels. Also in The Briefing, commitments agreed by Ticketmaster in the Netherlands escape a legal challenge, and New Zealand’s competition watchdog fails to convince a court to impose a first-ever post-closing merger divestment order.

item.title: Antitrust enforcers watchful of rising fuel prices
item.description: Competition agencies across Europe are monitoring fuel markets for potential antitrust breaches in light of supply-chain disruptions linked to the war in Iran.

item.title: EU seeks expanded influence over foreign investment control in new industrial bill
item.description: The European Commission’s legislative proposals to strengthen the region’s industrial base would give the bloc power to intervene in national foreign investment reviews targeting “strategic” sectors, including batteries and critical raw materials.

item.title: Apple seeks to decertify £785 million App Store lawsuit
item.description: Apple is attempting to use a recent UK Supreme Court ruling to reverse the certification of an opt-out collective action claim seeking compensation on behalf of over 13,000 app developers.

item.title: DOJ “sceptical” of Live Nation breakup, settles for behavioural fix
item.description: The Department of Justice has resolved its monopolisation suit against Live Nation with behavioural commitments, confounding many states and a federal judge who said they were blindsided by the mid-trial resolution.

item.title: Fertile ground: The Tipline for 9 March 2026
item.description: The US plaintiffs’ bar understands that, like farming, planting windows can be very limited. Fire Creek Farms has filed a lawsuit accusing six fertiliser manufacturers of price-fixing just three days after Bloomberg reported the existence of a Department of Justice probe. Also in Tipline, a municipality in Mississippi defends its zoning restrictions against a Sherman Act suit brought by Airbnb.&nb...
